kind: A screen on the server's test bed, two seeds, 24,000 updates: a racing loop (--stack-loop-exits), whose output neurons sum the evidence of every pass of the loop, beside the looped bed of the same recipe.
why: In cortex a decision is a race: neurons for each option sum evidence, and the choice is made when one leads by enough, so easy choices are fast and hard ones slow. A loop that runs the same passes for every byte cannot spend more on the hard bytes: at full size a third pass was 0.0008 better than two (full_size_loop_passes.json), 0.0016 better on new contexts and 0.0257 worse on near copies, so it helped some bytes and hurt others. A racing loop lets the output neurons hear the end of every pass and sum it; each pass's summed evidence learns to predict the byte by itself (the mean of their losses beside the top's), and a byte can then be decided at the first pass whose evidence leads by a margin. This is also the reasoning core of the one-model plan (volley-one): a loop that runs until it is sure, and one hop of lookup per pass. This screen asks two things before a loop that stops is built: what summing the passes does to the top's score, and how early the bytes settle.

arms.race: sched/bin/arm.sh stack --lr 1.2e-3 --seed 2000X --stack-loop 1,4,3 --pulse-budget 264000 --stack-loop-exits (--loop-exit-weight 1.0): the looped bed with exits after its first and second passes; 5,249,060 parameters, as the looped bed (the output neurons are shared by the passes)

base: lp-24k-s1 1.466405 and lp-24k-s2 1.467507: the looped bed without exits, the same seeds, rate, budget and length (code v17r).
runs: race-24k-s1 and race-24k-s2 (seeds 20001 and 20002), 24,000 updates of 16 x 256 bytes on streams, on GPU 0 at priority 37, on a new code copy of the commit that records this (v18d, launch-checked on the server's CPU first).
measure: arm.sh's score (experiments/eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, averaged weights): the evidence of all passes, paired with the base of its seed (compare_stream_scores.py) and split by context (gap_by_piece.py, near 240, far 8,192). Then experiments/loop_exits.py on the same streams: the bits of each pass's summed evidence, of the best pass for every byte, and the halting curve (mean bits and mean passes when each byte is decided at the first earlier pass whose margin reaches 0.5 to 12 bits). Every pass runs for every byte in this screen, so the curve measures how early bytes settle, not what a loop that stops saves.
reading: (1) Summing the passes costs nothing at the top if the mean paired gap to the base over the two seeds is no more than 0.003 against the racing loop; a lead of at least 0.005 on both seeds is a gain of its own and is reported as one. (2) Bytes settle early if on both seeds some margin decides with at most 2.5 passes on the mean (of 3) at no more than 0.002 bits above the racing loop's own score of all passes. If (1) and (2) hold, the loop that stops is built next (a decided byte's stream is held at every later pass and its pulses there are not spent) and is screened at equal mean pulses against the looped bed, in a record written then; its hop test joins hop_generalization.json by an amendment. If (2) fails, the racing loop rests, and only (1) is reported.
seen_before_recording: tests/test_loop_exits.py on small stacks (without exits the loop is unchanged; the exits' evidence is what the output neurons fire for each pass's stream; the stream is the same however it is cut; the earlier passes learn through their own evidence). No racing loop has trained.
